Date: 12/8/26

This document puts the cost of a negative-steering run next to the cost of the
structure predictors in `structure-prediction-benchmarking`, on the same 18
Tier-1 HMA decoy and AVR targets and the same cluster hardware.

The comparison is not single-valued. A benchmark run is 5 seeds × 5
diffusion samples = 25 predictions (ESMFold2 emits 5). A negative-steering run
is a cold start plus, if the cold start fails, `negsteer_n_designs` steering
sets × 3 seeds × 5 samples, with a re-prediction for every design whose
mutations needed reverting. Cost per run therefore scales with the number of
steering sets, and cost per prediction does not. The figure reports per-run cost
and the prediction count that explains it, and the paired tests below report
per-prediction cost.

Six steering cohorts are shown, because the parameter that dominates cost is
`negsteer_n_designs`, the steering-set count, and it was set differently across
all of them.

* 3, 5, 10, 20 and 50 steering sets, the same 18-target benchmark, all else
  held fixed. The 20-set point is the shipped benchmark under
  `experiments/benchmarking/`. The 3, 5, 10 and 50-set points are the dose
  sweep under `experiments/dose-sweep/`. Only the dose changes across these
  five, so they isolate the effect of `negsteer_n_designs` cleanly. The
  per-run scaling below is read from them.
* 3 steering sets on a different target set entirely. These are the 128
  designed sequences of the AVR-PikF campaign (`crystal_full_test_contig` in
  `receptor-resurfacing-pipeline`), at a median of 50 predictions per run.
  This is the setting the pipeline ships with. It is not the same run as the
  dose sweep's own 3-set point on the 18 benchmark targets, even though the
  dose is the same number.

The campaign differs from the benchmark cohorts in more than its target set.
Its candidate pool is smaller, 10 against 12. Its protected set comes from the
design region rather than the true interface. It sets
`negsteer_no_kernels: true`, and it runs many sequences at once
(`max_boltz2_parallel: 24`), which can inflate wall-clock through contention.

Its per-prediction figure is close to the dose sweep's own 3-set point even
so, 20.5 s against 22.9 s. The gap between them is therefore mostly sampling
depth rather than that configuration difference.

MSA search is counted, but not in wall-clock. For the three models that share
one pooled ColabFold/MMseqs2 search (Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 with an MSA, and
ColabFold), the reported time is `predict_wall_s + search_cpu_s`. That is
wall-clock for the GPU prediction step, plus CPU time for the search. The
search's own wall-clock would be the wrong number here. This run's
shared-storage node was contended and ran at low CPU utilisation while the
search waited on I/O. That inflates wall-clock without inflating the compute
actually spent, and CPU time is insulated from it. AlphaFold2-Multimer and AlphaFold3 run search
and prediction in one process and need no correction, since their own
wall-clock already includes it. Every no-MSA combo pays no search cost at all.
This mixes two units into one axis, which is a real caveat rather than an
oversight.
read the three shared-search MSA points as wall-clock-plus-CPU-cost, not as a
wall-clock time a clock on the wall would have shown.

Wall-clock for steering is every stage of the run summed (plan, predict-one,
collect, reversion, harvest, finalize, aggregate, metrics), not just the GPU
time. Both cohorts ran on the `jic-gpu` queue with `--gres=gpu:1`, so they are
comparable.

Regenerate the input CSV with:

```bash
python3 analysis/03-compute-cost/stage_runtime_comparison.py
```

## 1. Setup

```{python}
import math
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path.cwd()
if not (HERE / "runtime_comparison.csv").exists():
    HERE = Path("analysis/03-compute-cost")

rt = pd.read_csv(HERE / "runtime_comparison.csv")

NEGSTEER_20 = "Boltz-2 + negative steering (steering sets = 20)"
# The campaign's own 3-set point, NOT the dose sweep's 3-set point on the 18
# benchmark targets -- the two share a number but not a target set, and only
NEGSTEER_CAMPAIGN_3 = "Boltz-2 + negative steering, AVR-PikF campaign (steering sets = 3)"
# The variant is shown by colour, so the y axis carries the bare model name and the
# same model can appear more than once.
VARIANT_COLOR = {
    "no_msa": "#4C72B0",
    "msa": "#C44E52",
    "restraints": "#8172B2",
    "negsteer": "#55A868",
}
VARIANT_LABEL = {
    "no_msa": "No MSA",
    "msa": "MSA",
    "restraints": "restraints from the reference",
    "negsteer": "negative steering",
}

TIME_TICKS = [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200]        # minutes
PER_PRED_TICKS = [2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500]  # seconds

FIGDIR = HERE / "thesis-figures"
FIGDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def save_fig(fig, name):
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR / f"{name}.png", dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight", pad_inches=0.05)


def readable_log(axis, ticks):
    axis.set_ticks(ticks)
    axis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:g}"))
    axis.set_minor_locator(plt.NullLocator())
```

## 2. Cost per run

One point per model and variant, the median across the targets that model ran.
Spread is small relative to the differences between models. The tightest
combos vary by seconds and the widest by tens of minutes. Drawing it obscured
the comparison, so it is reported in the table instead.

```{python}
med = (rt.groupby(["model", "variant"])
         .agg(elapsed_min=("elapsed_min", "median"),
              sec_per_prediction=("sec_per_prediction", "median"),
              n_predictions=("n_predictions", "median"),
              n=("target", "size"))
         .reset_index()
         .sort_values("elapsed_min")
         .reset_index(drop=True))

ys = np.arange(len(med))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.0, 5.2))

ax.scatter(med["elapsed_min"], ys, s=78,
           color=[VARIANT_COLOR[a] for a in med["variant"]],
           edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.7, zorder=3)

# The two steering rows are far longer than any model name, so they wrap rather
# than push the plotting area off the page.
ax.set_yticks(ys)
ax.set_yticklabels([m.replace(" (steering", "\n(steering") for m in med["model"]],
                   fontsize=10)
ax.set_ylim(-0.8, len(med) - 0.4)
ax.invert_yaxis()   # fastest at the top
ax.set_xscale("log")
readable_log(ax.xaxis, TIME_TICKS)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=9.5)
ax.set_xlabel("Median wall-clock per run (minutes, log scale)", fontsize=10)
ax.grid(axis="x", ls=":", color="#CCCCCC", lw=0.6, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

# Predictions per run, as a right-hand column. Without it the ranking invites
# the wrong reading, since steering's run buys an order of magnitude more
# predictions than any benchmark run does.
trans = ax.get_yaxis_transform()
for y, n in zip(ys, med["n_predictions"]):
    ax.text(1.05, y, f"{int(n)}", transform=trans, ha="left", va="center",
            fontsize=9.5, clip_on=False)
ax.text(1.05, -0.85, "predictions\nper run", transform=trans, ha="left",
        va="center", fontsize=9.5, style="italic", clip_on=False)

handles = [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="none", marker="o", markersize=8,
                      mfc=VARIANT_COLOR[a], mec="black", mew=0.7)
           for a in ["no_msa", "msa", "restraints", "negsteer"]]
ax.legend(handles, [VARIANT_LABEL[a] for a in ["no_msa", "msa", "restraints", "negsteer"]],
          loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.01), ncol=2, frameon=False,
          fontsize=9.5, borderaxespad=0.0)
save_fig(fig, "compute_cost_comparison")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
spread = (rt.groupby(["model", "variant"])
            .agg(n=("target", "size"),
                 predictions=("n_predictions", "median"),
                 median_min=("elapsed_min", "median"),
                 min_min=("elapsed_min", "min"),
                 max_min=("elapsed_min", "max"),
                 median_s_per_pred=("sec_per_prediction", "median"),
                 median_peak_rss_gb=("peak_rss_gb", "median"))
            .round(1).sort_values("median_min").reset_index())
spread
```

- Once the MSA models carry their true search cost, negative steering is no
  longer the most expensive method here at any dose up to 20 sets. AlphaFold3,
  Boltz-2, AlphaFold2-Multimer, Boltz-1 and ColabFold with an MSA all land
  between 144 and 185 min, against 111 min for 20-set steering. Only the
  50-set dose sweep point, at 256 min, is more expensive than every MSA combo.
- Steering is cheaper per run than every MSA-based combination at every dose
  up to 20 sets (19, 29, 54 and 111 min against a 144-185 min MSA range). It
  costs more only at 50 sets, the far end of the dose sweep rather than
  anything the pipeline ships with.
- Per-prediction cost holds flat across the whole dose sweep, 20.3 to 22.9 s
  regardless of dose. The 305-vs-50-predictions-per-run gap between the 20-set
  benchmark and the 3-set AVR-PikF campaign is sampling depth, not
  per-prediction overhead: 22.1 s against 20.5 s.
- The overhead of steering itself is modest. Steering runs at 20.3 to 22.9 s per
  prediction against unsteered Boltz-2's 14.0 s. Planning, contact analysis,
  reversion and final metrics therefore add 45 to 64% on top of the raw
  Boltz-2 call. That overhead is essentially flat across dose.
- Some units never steer. Three of the 18 benchmark targets and 22 of the 128
  campaign sequences had a cold start that passed on every seed, so the run
  exited after 15 predictions. Cost is conditional on the cold start failing.

## 3. Cost against memory

The thesis figure. Wall-clock and peak memory on the same axes, so the two
resources that bound throughput can be read together. Negative steering sits
among the predictors rather than in a figure of its own.

Memory comes from different tooling per cohort (see
`stage_runtime_comparison.py`), and the two measurements agree closely where
they overlap, so the axis is comparable across every point. It is host RAM, not
VRAM, which is usually the real constraint.

Reference-restrained points share the No MSA colour, as they are a no-MSA variant,
and carry `(constr)` in their label. All five benchmark steering points are
plotted (steering sets 3, 5, 10, 20, 50), since all five ran the same 18
targets as the predictors they sit beside. The campaign's own 3-set point is
excluded, since it was measured on a different target set entirely and is not
comparable with the predictors here. Its cost is reported in the per-run
section above.

```{python}
SCATTER_COLOR = {"no_msa": VARIANT_COLOR["no_msa"], "restraints": VARIANT_COLOR["no_msa"],
                 "msa": VARIANT_COLOR["msa"], "negsteer": VARIANT_COLOR["negsteer"]}
SCATTER_LEGEND = [("no_msa", "No MSA"), ("msa", "MSA"),
                  ("negsteer", "Negative steering\n(steering sets)")]

med2 = (rt[rt["model"] != NEGSTEER_CAMPAIGN_3]
          .groupby(["model", "variant"])
          .agg(runtime=("elapsed_min", "median"),
               memory=("peak_rss_gb", "median"))
          .reset_index())


def scatter_label(model, variant):
    if variant == "negsteer":
        # Bare count; the legend says these are steering sets.
        return "Boltz-2 (%s)" % model.split("= ")[1].rstrip(")")
    return f"{model} (constr)" if variant == "restraints" else model


med2["label"] = [scatter_label(m, a) for m, a in zip(med2["model"], med2["variant"])]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.4, 6.4))
for variant in ["msa", "restraints", "no_msa", "negsteer"]:
    sub = med2[med2["variant"] == variant]
    ax.scatter(sub["runtime"], sub["memory"], s=90, color=SCATTER_COLOR[variant],
               alpha=0.65, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6,
               zorder=5 if variant == "negsteer" else 4)

# Fixed placement, no jitter and no leader lines: every label sits directly
# beside its own point in one of the four cardinal directions. Default is
# left; these (model, variant) pairs are the explicit exceptions.
# Boltz-1 msa, AlphaFold3 msa and ColabFold msa are the three red (MSA) points.
LABEL_RIGHT = {("Boltz-2", "restraints"), ("Boltz-1", "restraints"),
               ("Boltz-1", "msa"), ("ColabFold", "msa")}
LABEL_ABOVE_KEY = {("AlphaFold3", "msa")}
LABEL_BELOW_KEY = set()
LABEL_ABOVE = {"Boltz-2 (5)"}     # keyed on label text (negsteer rows share "Boltz-2")
LABEL_BELOW = {"Boltz-2 (3)", "Boltz-2 (10)", "Boltz-2 (20)"}
LABEL_RIGHT_TEXT = {"Boltz-2 (50)"}

OFFSET = 9  # points, same distance in every direction
for _, r in med2.iterrows():
    key = (r["model"], r["variant"])
    text = r["label"]
    if key in LABEL_RIGHT or text in LABEL_RIGHT_TEXT:
        dx, dy, ha, va = OFFSET, 0, "left", "center"
    elif text in LABEL_ABOVE or key in LABEL_ABOVE_KEY:
        dx, dy, ha, va = 0, OFFSET, "center", "bottom"
    elif text in LABEL_BELOW or key in LABEL_BELOW_KEY:
        dx, dy, ha, va = 0, -OFFSET, "center", "top"
    else:
        dx, dy, ha, va = -OFFSET, 0, "right", "center"
    ax.annotate(text, (r["runtime"], r["memory"]), fontsize=7.5,
                xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", ha=ha, va=va,
                zorder=6)

ax.set_xscale("log")
readable_log(ax.xaxis, TIME_TICKS)
ax.set_xlabel("Median wall-clock per run (minutes, log scale)")
ax.set_ylabel("Median peak resident memory (GB)")
# Extended well past the data range on both ends, so every edge label (left:
# AlphaFold3 no-MSA at 1.9 min; right: ColabFold msa, Boltz-1 msa and
# Boltz-2 (50) at 185-256 min) sits clear of the axes border/tick labels
# rather than crowding it.
ax.set_xlim(0.9, 550)
handles = [plt.Line2D([], [], ls="none", marker="o", markersize=8,
                      mfc=SCATTER_COLOR[a], mec="black", mew=0.7, alpha=0.65)
           for a, _ in SCATTER_LEGEND]
ax.legend(handles, [lab for _, lab in SCATTER_LEGEND], loc="center left",
          bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5), frameon=True, fontsize=10)
save_fig(fig, "compute_cost_tradeoff")
plt.show()
```

- Negative steering costs no more memory than the Boltz-2 it wraps, 4.6 to
  5.1 GB depending on dose against 5.0 GB unsteered, and flat across the whole
  dose sweep. Memory is set by the prediction model, so the engine's extra
  stages are not what bounds how many can run at once.
- At every dose from 3 to 50 sets, steering uses 7-8x less memory than
  AlphaFold2-Multimer while spanning most of its wall-clock range. Under a
  memory cap it therefore parallelises far better than a wall-clock
  comparison alone suggests.

## 4. Is the per-prediction cost of steering below the MSA models?

Paired within target, since targets differ in size and the same targets are run
by every method. The paired quantity is the ratio of negative steering's
per-prediction cost to the other method's, so a ratio below 1 means steering is
cheaper per prediction. Reported as the median ratio with a bootstrap 95%
interval, plus an exact two-sided sign test on the paired differences.

```{python}
def sign_test(diffs):
    """Exact two-sided sign test p-value. Ties dropped."""
    d = np.asarray([x for x in diffs if x != 0])
    n, k = len(d), int((np.asarray(d) > 0).sum())
    if n == 0:
        return float("nan")
    tail = sum(math.comb(n, i) for i in range(min(k, n - k) + 1))
    return min(1.0, 2 * tail / 2 ** n)


def boot_median_ci(x, n_boot=10000, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    draws = np.median(rng.choice(x, size=(n_boot, len(x)), replace=True), axis=1)
    return np.percentile(draws, [2.5, 97.5])


# Paired on target, so this uses the 20-set benchmark cohort. The 3-set campaign
# runs 128 designed sequences against one effector rather than the 18 solved
# complexes, so it shares no targets with the benchmark and cannot be paired
# against it. It appears in the figure and the table above, not here.
ns = rt[rt["model"] == NEGSTEER_20].set_index("target")["sec_per_prediction"]
rows = []
for _, r in med.iterrows():
    if r["variant"] == "negsteer":
        continue
    other = rt[(rt["model"] == r["model"]) & (rt["variant"] == r["variant"])] \
        .set_index("target")["sec_per_prediction"]
    shared = ns.index.intersection(other.index)
    ratio = (ns[shared] / other[shared]).values
    lo, hi = boot_median_ci(ratio)
    p = sign_test((ns[shared] - other[shared]).values)
    rows.append({
        "vs": f"{r['model']} ({VARIANT_LABEL[r['variant']]})",
        "n paired": len(shared),
        "median ratio": round(float(np.median(ratio)), 2),
        "95% CI": f"{lo:.2f}–{hi:.2f}",
        "p (sign test)": "<0.0001" if p < 1e-4 else f"{p:.4f}",
        "verdict": ("steering cheaper" if hi < 1 else
                    "steering costlier" if lo > 1 else "indistinguishable"),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

- Steering is cheaper per prediction than every MSA-based combination, and by
  a wide margin now the search cost is counted properly. Against
  AlphaFold2-Multimer, AlphaFold3, Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 with an MSA and
  ColabFold, the ratio is 0.05-0.06 in every case, all intervals well clear
  of 1.
- Among the no-MSA models it is cheaper only than ESMFold2, at 0.37. The
  largest gap in the table is against AlphaFold3, at 4.60x more expensive,
  because AlphaFold3 without an MSA is the fastest method here at 1.9 min a
  run. Against the
  rest it is 1.2 to 1.6x more expensive per prediction, the expected price of
  the extra Boltz-2 calls and the engine's own stages.
- So the claim holds per prediction at every dose. Per run it holds up to 20
  sets and fails only at 50, where steering deliberately samples deeper than
  any single prediction does.

Wall-clock is execution time rather than time-to-result, so queueing is
excluded. One benchmark target has no usable trace row, so the benchmark combos
cover 17 of 18 targets against steering's 18. Both cohorts ran on the same queue
and GPU allocation, though not necessarily on identical nodes. A fixed
sampling budget dominates the steering cost, 20 designs by 3 seeds, and it was
never tuned. This is therefore a cost of this configuration rather than a
floor for the method.
